correctness.rationale: For each p>1 the finite-dimensional mass-weighted p-energy gradient flow has global unique solutions. The star incidence map realizes arbitrary edge differences. Maximizing the weighted ℓ1 directional subgradient yields the exact upper Dini derivative; the bound is attained at a one-edge profile even though all other absolute values are nonsmooth. Nonpositive coefficients are necessary and sufficient for all-time contraction, and normalization of the edge gauge produces the exact reciprocal-mass feasibility criterion. Exact rational tests and fractional-p/Euler checks corroborate the algebra without replacing its proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp p-independent mass threshold and exact normalized Dini generator were compared against four primary full-text sources, a relevant graph-cut abstract, targeted literature searches, available published research summaries and accessible prior mathematical findings. The closest broad nonlinear p-semigroup source proves vertex-space contraction, not independent weighted edge-variation dissipativity. The counting-mass p=2 tree special case cannot imply the six-leaf central-mass phase transition and all-p statement. No directly covering implication was found; older implicit dissipativity formulations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The graph p-heat is a natural nonlinear diffusion on measured networks; sharp variation control is important to distinguish true smoothing from branch-induced instability. The result gives a complete all-exponent classification for arbitrary positive mass/weight profiles, an exactly attained infinitesimal invariant, and a critical central-mass law that changes the qualitative stability of stars of arbitrarily high degree. That is more than a numerical table, arbitrary parameter slice, or straightforward restatement of vertex-space contraction; it identifies a structural mechanism absent in counting-mass tree results.
